descripcion_es: First mention, unique things and basic uses with no article.
resumen: A/an is the indefinite article and the is the definite article. Unlike Spanish, English leaves out the article when talking about something in general with plural or uncountable nouns.

explicacion.texto: A is used before a consonant sound (a book, a university) and an before a vowel sound (an apple, an hour). What counts is the sound, not the letter.

filas: the sun, the sea, the internet
Plural and uncountable nouns in general
I like cats. Milk is good for you.
at breakfast, in English, play football, on Monday

items: Fixed expressions with no article: at home, at work, go to bed, go to school, by bus.
The is pronounced /ðə/ before a consonant and /ði/ before a vowel sound (the apple).
Jobs always take a/an in the singular: He's a doctor (not “He's doctor”).

ejemplos.frase: I bought a shirt and a jacket. The jacket was very cheap.
ejemplos.traduccion: Compré una camisa y una chaqueta. La chaqueta era muy barata.

ejemplos.frase: We usually have lunch at two.
The moon is very bright tonight.
ejemplos.traduccion: La luna brilla mucho esta noche.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In general statements, uncountable nouns do not take the.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She goes to the school by the bus.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: She goes to school by bus.

ejercicios.explicacion: Two rules from the card apply. First: jobs always take a/an in the singular, although Spanish says “es arquitecta” without an article. Second: an is used before a vowel sound. The clue is the pronunciation of “architect”, which begins with the sound /ɑː/, a vowel sound. That is why it is “She's an architect”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Architect begins with a vowel sound.

errores_previstos.explicacion: “Architect” begins with a vowel sound, so the article is “an”, not “a”.
To say what someone's job is, use the indefinite article a/an, not “the”.

ejercicios.frase: He studies at ___ university in Madrid.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule on the card that the sound counts, not the letter. The clue is that “university” is spelt with u, but it is pronounced /juː/, like “you”, which is a consonant sound. That is why we say “a university”, even though the first letter is a vowel. The same happens with “a European country” or “a one-way ticket”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: University begins with the sound /j/, a consonant sound.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estudia en una universidad de Madrid.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Although it begins with the letter u, “university” sounds /juː/, which is a consonant sound: “a university”.
It refers to any university in Madrid, mentioned for the first time: use the indefinite article.

ejercicios.frase: The train leaves in half ___ hour.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the sound rule: an before a vowel sound. The clue is that in “hour” the h is silent, so the word begins with the sound /aʊ/. That is why it is “half an hour”, which is also a very common expression. The same happens with “an honest man” or “an heir”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In hour the h is not pronounced: vowel sound.
ejercicios.traduccion: El tren sale dentro de media hora.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The h in “hour” is not pronounced: the word begins with a vowel sound and takes “an”.
“Half the hour” does not mean “thirty minutes” (Spanish “media hora”); the fixed expression is “half an hour”.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with a, an or the.
ejercicios.frase: I saw a film last night. ___ film was about a pianist.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: a/an for the first mention and the for something already mentioned or known. The clue is the previous sentence, “I saw a film”, which introduces the film; now we talk about that same film again, which is now specific for the listener. That is why it is “The film”, with a capital letter because it begins the sentence. It is the same mechanism as Spanish “una película… la película”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Anoche vi una película. La película trataba de un pianista.

errores_previstos.explicacion: “A film” would introduce a different film; the sentence is about the one already mentioned, so it is “The”.
“This” is not an article and the exercise asks for a, an or the; for the second mention the article is “The”.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table for unique things: they take the (the sun, the sea, the internet). The clue is “sun”: there is only one, so it cannot be just any sun. That is why it is “The sun rises in the east”, where “the east” also takes the article because it is a unique compass point. In this case Spanish works the same way.
ejercicios.traduccion: El sol sale por el este.

por_opcion.A: Incorrect: “a sun” would be any sun among many; when talking about ours, which is unique, use “the”.
por_opcion.The: Correct: a unique thing, known to everyone.
por_opcion.An: Incorrect: as well as not being the right article, “sun” begins with a consonant sound and would never take “an”.

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct option (– means no article).
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: no article with plural and uncountable nouns when talking in general. The clue is the verb “like”, which expresses a general preference, and “coffee”, which is uncountable. That is why it is “I don't like coffee”, with nothing before it. Spanish says “el café”, and that “el” is what leads people to add “the” by mistake.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: General preference with an uncountable noun: no article.

por_opcion.the: Incorrect here: “the coffee” would refer to a specific coffee (for example, the coffee at that café); for a general preference there is no article.
por_opcion.a: Incorrect: “coffee” as a substance is uncountable and does not take “a”. Only in speech do people say “a coffee” meaning “a cup of coffee”, which is not the meaning here.
por_opcion.–: Correct: general preference with an uncountable noun, no article.

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the correct option (– means no article).
ejercicios.frase: We go to ___ bed at eleven.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the card's list of fixed expressions with no article: at home, at work, go to bed, go to school, by bus. The clue is “go to ___ bed”, which means going to sleep and is one of those expressions. That is why it is “We go to bed at eleven”. With the article, “the bed” would be the specific piece of furniture, not the act of going to sleep.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Go to bed is a fixed expression with no article.

por_opcion.the: Incorrect: “go to the bed” would mean walking over to the piece of furniture, not going to sleep.
por_opcion.a: Incorrect: “go to a bed” makes no sense as going to sleep.
por_opcion.–: Correct: “go to bed” is a fixed expression with no article.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: the for something known to both speakers. The clue is the situation: the speaker asks for a specific door to be closed, the one in the room they are in, and both know which one it is. That is why it is “close the door”. With “a door” you would be asking to close any door at all, which makes no sense.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A specific door that both people know: the.

por_opcion.a: Incorrect: “a door” would be any door; the sentence is about a specific one in front of both of them.
por_opcion.the: Correct: a specific door, identifiable from the context.
por_opcion.an: Incorrect: “door” begins with a consonant sound and, in addition, the definite article is needed here.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule on the card that jobs always take a/an in the singular. The clue is “is teacher”: after the verb be we say what someone's job is, and in English that requires an article, although Spanish does not use one. As “teacher” begins with a consonant, the correct sentence is “My sister is a teacher”.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: it is a literal copy of Spanish “es profesora”; in English a job takes “a”.
“The teacher” would mean she is the specific teacher being talked about, not her job.
“Teacher” begins with a consonant sound: it takes “a”, not “an”.

ejercicios.frase: I eat an banana every morning.
respuestas: I eat a banana every morning.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the sound rule: a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound. The clue is “banana”, which begins with /b/, a consonant sound. That is why it is “a banana”. The mistake usually comes from using “an” with any fruit (“an apple”, “an orange”), which do begin with a vowel.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Banana begins with a consonant: a.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me como un plátano todas las mañanas.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I eat an banana every morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: “banana” begins with a consonant, so the article is “a”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I eat the banana every morning.
errores_previstos.explicacion: “The banana” would be a specific banana already known; here it is any banana every morning.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: no article with plurals when talking in general. The clue is that the sentence defines cats as a species, not some specific cats. That is why it is “Cats are independent animals”. Spanish says “los gatos”, but in English “the cats” only refers to particular cats (for example, the neighbour's).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: When talking about cats in general, the is not used.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: “the cats” refers to specific cats, not to cats in general.
The article is also unnecessary before “independent animals”: the sentence describes cats in general.

ejercicios.frase: I play the tennis on Saturdays.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the table: meals, languages, sports and days take no article. The clue is the verb “play” followed by the name of the sport, “tennis”. That is why it is “I play tennis on Saturdays”. Spanish says “al tenis”, and that “el” pushes people to write “the”. Playing an instrument is different: it does take “the” (play the guitar).

errores_previstos.respuesta: I play the tennis on Saturdays.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: sports take no article.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I play tennis on the Saturdays.
errores_previstos.explicacion: As well as removing “the” from the sport, days of the week do not take an article either: “on Saturdays”.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the sound rule: an before a vowel sound. The clue is that the article goes before the adjective “interesting”, not the noun “book”, and it is the word that follows the article that decides. As “interesting” begins with a vowel, “an” is used. The order is subject “This” + “is” + article + adjective + noun; the question “Is this an interesting book” is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Interesting begins with a vowel: an.

errores_previstos.explicacion: In English the adjective goes before the noun; also, before “book” the article would be “a”.
The verb “is” goes after the subject “This”, not at the end.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the list of fixed expressions with no article: at home, at work, go to bed. The clue is “at home”, which means being in your own home and never takes “the”. The order is subject “My father” + “is” + “at home”. The question “Is my father at home”, with the verb before the subject, is also accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: At home is said with no article.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The preposition “at” goes before “home”: “at home”.
This order copies a Spanish emphatic structure; in English it is subject + verb + “at home”.

descripcion_larga_es: The articles a/an and the, and the cases in which English uses no article at all. They appear in almost every sentence, so a mistake is repeated again and again. Spanish speakers find them difficult because Spanish uses an article to generalise (Spanish “me gusta el café”) and leaves it out with jobs (Spanish “es médico”), exactly the opposite of English.

contexto.que_es: English has an indefinite article, a/an, and a definite article, the, which does not change for gender or number. There are also many cases with no article, especially when talking about something in general with plural or uncountable nouns. The choice between a and an depends on the sound of the next word, not the letter.
contexto.por_que_importa: They are in almost every sentence, so a systematic mistake is noticed immediately and is repeated dozens of times in a text. Some mistakes change the meaning: “I love the chocolate” talks about a specific chocolate, not chocolate in general. They are also a classic in exam exercises.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: A/an appears when mentioning something for the first time and with jobs; the, when returning to something already mentioned or with unique things (the sun); no article, to generalise and in fixed expressions (at home, go to bed, by bus). Spanish speakers tend to put “the” where Spanish uses “el” to generalise (“the life is…”) and to forget “a” with jobs (“he is engineer”).
